title: The ALMA-QUARKS survey: Extensive detection of acetamide in multiple high-mass star-forming regions
question: How prevalent is acetamide (CH3CONH2) across hot molecular cores in high-mass star-forming regions, and how do its abundance and formation pathways relate to formamide (NH2CHO)?

recipe.method: Inspect spectral cubes line-by-line and extract spectra from positions offset from the continuum peak where lines show Gaussian profiles and avoid strong continuum absorption and severe line blending

recipe.goal: Identify molecular lines and model synthetic spectra
recipe.method: Simulate observed emission in GILDAS under LTE, fit Gaussian line profiles, subtract overlapping species using best-fit LTE synthetic spectra for partially blended lines, and require >=5 unblended transitions with S/N >= 3sigma for secure detection
key_parameters: Five model parameters: source size (fixed to deconvolved continuum angular size), line width (from Gaussian fitting), velocity offset (calibrated via CH3OH at 218440.063 MHz), rotational temperature (free), and column density (free)
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) and uniform source-filling emission

recipe.goal: Derive excitation temperatures, column densities, and upper limits
recipe.method: Use rotational diagrams for molecules with at least three unblended transitions spanning a broad energy range; for species with fewer transitions or narrow energy range, fix T_ex to the other amide and calculate N from individual lines; scale NH2^13CHO column densities by the 12C/13C ratio to obtain NH2CHO column densities; derive 3sigma upper limits for the 42 non-detections
key_parameters: Source sizes theta_source from 0.9 to 3.8 arcsec (Table 2) and 12C/13C ratios from Table 1
assumptions: LTE, optically thin emission for CH3CONH2 and NH2^13CHO, and equal excitation temperatures between CH3CONH2 and NH2^13CHO when one cannot be independently fitted

recipe.goal: Map spatial distributions of amide emission
recipe.method: Generate integrated intensity (moment-0) maps of unblended NH2CHO and CH3CONH2 transitions and overlay on 1.3 mm continuum emission

recipe.goal: Analyze chemical correlation and abundance ratios
recipe.method: Normalize NH2CHO and CH3CONH2 column densities to CH3OH, combine with literature sources, fit a power-law correlation, and compare abundance ratios with astrochemical models and laboratory ice simulations
assumptions: 20% uncertainty assumed for literature abundances where not specified

evidence.quote: Acetamide has been detected in 10 cores, markedly expanding the inventory of known emitters.
Both NH$_{2}$CHO and CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ were detected in ten HMCs, increasing the number of known CH$_{3}$CONH$_{2}$ sources to 17 and providing the most extensive sample to date for this molecule.
